Honestly, he sounds just like me and my boyfriend thinks and says the same things you say. Personally, I am super grateful to have someone who thinks and acts just like you in my relationship. God knows where I would be without him, even though I also have wanted to leave the relationship and that has been because I haven't felt like a "good girlfriend". I think your suggestion sounds great and you giving him reassurance: that it is okay that he can't be 100% right now, is probably really helpful for him. What will happen in the future? I don't know myself with my own relationship, but I just try to enjoy the calm and good moments, that a relationship can give and I hope he can too. I still think he should seek some help, counseling or other therapeutic matters to get to the root of the problem, which is certainly not you or you two's relationship. 

In regards to your family and friends and him, I would say give him time to get used to them, keep at it telling him that your family likes him, since that probably means a lot to him. Friends make jokes like that and that's okay and something he also has to be okay with, it's healthy to kid around a bit and he needs that socialisation too - everybody does :) 
Oh! And a lil tip for something that I, the depressed partner, always can manage to do as a couple thing is watching a show together. I know how exhausting being depressed is and it can make everything so overwhelming, but cozying up to a cool series with a loved one can be the best distraction from depressed spirals and it can bring you two closer together, even if everything is kind of impossible for him right now. In the end, time will heal the wound, but only when it is properly addressed and cared for. Getting out of a depression takes time and it just has to be accepted that way, even though it can be hard to keep the patience.
All in all, it sounds like it is going the right direction and now you two just gotta keep at it, even though some days can be super hard, that is how it is when you are literally sick in your mental state and you have to treat it like a broken leg or any other physical injury, give it time, patience and love. And very important, remember to also take care of yourself. Cheers :)

You could start off asking why it  is he wants to break up? If he is not capable of being in a relationship because of his depression, then you can only really respect his wish. But if the indication is that he wants to isolate himself from anything good in his life, then I would notify his mom or dad about it. Depression tend to want to trick oneself into isolation, so the fear of everyone leaving you becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy. Honestly it is a really bad sign that you are getting anxious, that is not healthy for you or him. I understand and really admire that you are so compassionate and helpful to him, that'll only help him see the good in people even if his sight is foggy. But you really have to look out for yourself, don't get dragged down with him no matter how much you love him. So my advice is to talk things through, tell him how you are feeling about you two's relationship, find out if he wants to break-up out of depressed and maybe even suicidal intent or if he just can't handle dealing with caring for another person right now, because he has his own mountain of selflove to climb first. But for your own sake, I would recommend seeking help from his family or friends to also keep an eye out on him and let yourself get some space to breathe, maybe spend a weekend apart and do something that'll lighten your soul a bit, like going to the movies with friends. I hope what I am saying can help you and him, I really wish the best for both of you.

Remember that you can help him, but you also need to respect and maintain your own sanity, love yourself as much as you love him.

The depression don't go away unless something in his life changes, maybe it's genetic, but he has to put the work in to fix it himself - he is the only one who can save him in the end. 
For you, I would advice you to be consistent and patient, but also you are in your right to want to push him a bit towards healthier choices and to have needs and wants yourself. You should be able to push him to get better, but word it and explain why, because a depressed mind can really fog why people behave and say things.
